title.narrative: Provision of food assistance through cash transfer for affected communities in Jamaame District, Lower Juba, Somalia, prioritizing community-defined needs.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThis pilot initiative, funded through the Somali Humanitarian Fund (SHF) flagship allocation, aims to strengthen resilience and improve the well-being of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities in Jamaame District, Lower Juba. The project prioritizes the most vulnerable and underserved households, particularly those severely affected by climate-related shocks such as recurrent flooding and prolonged drought. Its core objective is to address food insecurity through the provision of multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA), helping to reduce food consumption gaps and prevent further displacement.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project adopts a participatory, community-driven approach that places local perspectives at the center of decision-making throughout the project cycle, including planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation. Strong emphasis is placed on community engagement and local ownership, with decision-making responsibilities decentralized to district and village levels to enhance accountability and ensure assistance reaches the most vulnerable populations. By leveraging indigenous knowledge, existing community structures, and locally available resources, the project seeks to deliver an effective and contextually appropriate response to ongoing food emergencies.ltbrgtImplemented over a six-month period, the project will support 590 households selected through a coordinated process with SHF-funded partners across protection, WASH, health, and nutrition sectors. Following household registration and verification, a consolidated beneficiary list will be submitted to SHF. Each eligible household will receive USD 100 per month for three consecutive months through mobile money transfers, in line with the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) rate for Jamaame District as established by the Cash Working Group. Payments will be delivered in three cycles, with post-distribution monitoring (PDM) conducted after each transfer. ltbrgtProject activities will be implemented in two target villages within Jamaame District: Wirkoy (Latitude: -0.027743, Longitude: 42.60036) and Towfiq (Latitude: -0.006412). SEA will work in close coordination with SHF partners and other humanitarian actors to promote efficient resource use and strong inter-sectoral linkages. The intervention will be aligned with ongoing efforts in health, nutrition, food security, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), and shelter to maximize overall impact and sustainability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
